chunks: The saying in the ruku' and the sujud is three tasbihat (glorifications), and five is better, and seven is best, and a single complete tasbihah suffices in the ruku' and the sujud for the sick and the one in a hurry.

So whoever reduces from the three tasbihat in his ruku' or in his sujud by one tasbihah, and he is not sick nor in a hurry, then he has reduced a third of his prayer. And whoever leaves off two tasbihat, then he has reduced two-thirds of his prayer.

And whoever does not do tasbih in his ruku' and his sujud, then there is no prayer for him unless he does tahlil, or does takbir, or sends blessings upon the Prophet and his family by the number of the tasbih, for indeed that suffices him.
And the two testimonies suffice in the tashahhud, so whatever is more than that is additional worship.
And the taslim in the prayer suffices once while facing the qibla, inclining one's eyes toward one's right.
And whoever is in a gathering of the people of opposition (non-Shia), he gives two taslims: a taslim to his right and a taslim to his left, as they do, out of taqiyya (precautionary dissimulation).

key_terms.تسبيحات: Tasbihat: glorifications of God, specifically saying 'subhan Allah' in ruku' and sujud
key_terms.تسليم: Taslim: the concluding salutation of the prayer
key_terms.تشهد: Tashahhud: the testimony of faith recited while sitting in the prayer
key_terms.تقية: Taqiyya: precautionary dissimulation, practicing the form of worship of other Muslims to avoid conflict

ai.seo_question: How many tasbihat should be said in ruku' and sujud according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of Sheikh al-Saduq provides detailed jurisprudential rulings on three aspects of prayer: the number of tasbihat in ruku' and sujud (three is the standard, five is better, seven is best, and one suffices for the sick or hurried), the sufficiency of the two testimonies in tashahhud, and the manner of performing taslim (once facing the qibla for normal circumstances, or twice when praying among non-Shia Muslims for taqiyya). The graduated penalties for reducing tasbihat underscore the importance of this act of worship within the prayer.

does tahlil (says la ilaha illa Allah)

en.bilal-muhammad: The saying in the ruku` and the sujud is three tasbihat (saying subhanAllah), and five is better, and seven is best, and the [single] complete tasbiha suffices in the unit and the sujud for the person who is sick and the one in a hurry.
So, whoever does less than the three tasbihat in his unit and in his sujud, and he is not sick and not in a hurry, then he has reduced a third of his salat.

Whoever leaves off two tasbiha, then he has reduced two thirds of his prayer. Whoever does not do tasbih [at all] in his unit and his sujud, then there is no salat for him unless he does tahlil (saying la ilaha illAllah) or does takbir or blesses the Prophet and his family by the number of the tasbih, for that suffices him.
The two testimonies suffice in the tashahhud, so what is more [than that] then it is [additional] worship (ta`abbud).
[As to] the taslim in the prayer, one time facing the qibla suffices, inclining one’s eye to one’s right.
Someone who is in a jama`a with the opponents (ahl al-khilaf) does taslim with two taslima, a taslima to his right and a taslima to his left, as they do, out of taqiyya.
